positives.subject: Golden-set membership in crates/cobre-sddp/tests/parity.rs is justified case by case, and no two of the five cases cover the same LP structure
positives.why: This is the answer to the golden-set question and it is a positive, not a candidate. The selection rationale is documented at the point of use: the case_dir doc in tests/common/parity_hash.rs states the five labels are deliberately non-sequential and pins each to distinct machinery, D06 to the variable-head FPHA average-storage coefficient on both incoming and outgoing storage columns, D15 to the NCS availability factor and the lower-bound-patches-NCS contract, D30 to multi-resolution monthly and quarterly decomposition, D34 to anticipated dispatch under non-uniform per-stage block counts, and D41 to energy import and export contract columns. It also states that the simpler d01 through d05 single-feature cases are covered at the behavioral tier in tests/deterministic.rs and that promoting a case into this golden set needs justification, which is the promotion rule testing-architecture.md section 5.3 asks for, already written down. The same module doc pre-empts the obvious reduction, recording that hash fields 4 through 6 are each an n_blks-dependent read kept specifically to surface an extraction, cost or base bug that a uniform-block case cannot detect and must not be dropped as duplicates. The ten test functions are two backends over those five cases, and the backend halves are not redundant either: the CLP module doc records that CLP's simplex legitimately reaches different-but-valid optima so its digests differ, which is why the baselines live in a separate parity_baselines_clp fixture directory and why a HiGHS digest cannot stand in for a CLP one. Worth noting for the reader that ten only materializes when both additive Cargo features are enabled, since each backend module is cfg-gated per feature and the default is highs alone. No reduction is available here that does not lose a distinct failure mode.

positives.subject: The determinism, rank-invariance and wire gates are correctly treated as informational and are not bloat

The Cobre determinism definition is reproducibility plus declaration-order invariance, which structurally requires running the same case more than once under different orderings and different world sizes, and a Phase-0a bit-for-bit gate reuses exactly this machinery.
